questions.q: According to the summary, what are the four continuous processes of the mind?
a: Consciousness, perception, sensation and reaction
Attention, memory, judgment and imagination
Breathing, sensing, thinking and sleeping
Desire, aversion, habit and identity
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists these four as the mind's continuous activity, alongside the body's constant flux.

questions.q: What does perception do in that sequence?
a: It decides whether what we encountered is positive or negative for us
It simply registers that something is happening
It produces a physical sensation of comfort or discomfort
It chooses to avoid what is unpleasant
questions.why: Lesson 1 assigns perception the job of judging whether something is positive or negative for us.

A breathing exercise used to quiet the mind
A set of rituals performed at a temple
A form of fasting practiced by monks
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines Sila as morality, a way of living that avoids harm and keeps peace with others.

questions.q: What advice does the summary give about work and Sila?
a: Earn a living from something that does not spread harm or hate
Avoid all paid work and rely on charity
Choose the highest-paying job regardless of its effects
Keep your moral rules separate from your job
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to seek work that does not perpetuate harm, naming gambling and drug sales as examples.

questions.q: What happens when you first try to meditate, according to the summary?
a: The inner chatter is hard to quiet, so you return your focus to breathing
The mind goes blank almost immediately
You fall into a deep, dreamless sleep
You begin to see vivid images of the past
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the mind wanders at first and that you should gently return to your breathing.
